objective: Develop the ability to use an arcing support run that allows the player to receive while already facing the team’s attacking direction.
groundSize: Channels approximately 20 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours.
setup:
Position a ball carrier on one side of the channel.
Position a support player five metres behind and inside the ball carrier.
Mark an arcing path with three guide cones.
Place a forward target at the opposite end of the channel.
Create a receiving gate at the end of the arc.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins moving forward at controlled speed.
The support player starts behind the ball carrier and runs an outward arc.
The support player continues around the guide cones and bends the run forward.
The ball carrier handballs into the receiving gate.
The support player receives while facing the forward target.
The receiver accelerates for three steps.
The receiver disposes to the forward target.
Players follow their disposal and rotate positions.
Repeat the pattern from both sides.
coachingPoints: Begin behind the football.
Maintain width during the early part of the arc.
Bend the run forward before receiving.
Keep vision on the ball carrier and the next target.
Arrive at the receiving gate at speed.
Present the hands early.
Receive with the hips and shoulders facing forward.
Continue the possession without stopping.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the support player starts behind the ball carrier.
Whether the arc creates useful width.
Whether the player turns forward before receiving.
Whether the handball leads the player.
Whether forward momentum continues after reception.
progressions: Remove the guide cones.
Add a defender between the ball carrier and support player.
Allow the support player to choose between an arc, overlap or underlap.
Require a kick after receiving.
Add a second forward target.
regressions: Reduce the width of the arc.
successIndicators: Begin from a genuine support position.
matchApplication: An arcing support run allows a player to receive without turning back towards pressure. It is valuable when exiting defensive 50, supporting along the boundary or connecting a handball chain into the corridor.

title: Blind-Side Breakaway Lead
objective: Teach players to begin outside an opponent’s direct vision and accelerate into an available receiving lane at the correct moment.
groundSize: Leading channels approximately 20 × 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position one attacker and defender approximately 18 metres from a kicker.
The defender begins facing the kicker.
The attacker begins one metre behind and slightly outside the defender’s shoulder.
Mark two possible receiving gates.
The kicker begins with a football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker scans the defender’s head and body orientation.
The kicker begins preparing to dispose.
While remaining outside the defender’s direct vision, the attacker adjusts position behind the defender.
When the defender looks towards the football, the attacker accelerates past either shoulder.
The kicker delivers into the selected receiving gate.
The defender turns and attempts to recover under controlled pressure.
The attacker marks and plays on towards a finishing target.
Players rotate through attacker, defender and kicker.
Repeat from both sides.
coachingPoints: Stay close enough to threaten both sides of the defender.
Avoid making unnecessary noise or early movement.
Watch the defender’s head and hips.
Accelerate when the defender’s vision is fixed on the football.
Take the shortest clear path past the defender.
Communicate with the kicker only when necessary.
Maintain separation through the receiving gate.
Continue moving after the mark.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker begins outside the defender’s direct vision.
Whether the movement is timed to the defender’s attention.
Whether the first steps create separation.
Whether the defender is able to recover immediately.
Whether the kicker recognises the correct release time.
progressions: Allow the defender full match-like tracking pressure.
Remove the receiving gates.
Add a second attacker using coordinated movement.
Require a kick after the mark.
Begin from a moving rather than stationary setup.
regressions: Increase the space between attacker and defender.
Rehearse the movement without a football delivery.
successIndicators: Time movement to the defender’s attention.
matchApplication: Blind-side movement helps forwards, midfielders and defenders lose close opponents by exploiting moments when those opponents are watching the football rather than their direct player.

title: Switchback Support Run
primarySkill: Changing support direction after the initial lane closes
objective: Develop the ability to abandon a closed support lane and redirect quickly into a second useful receiving position.
groundSize: Areas approximately 22 × 15 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position a ball carrier in a central lane.
Place one support player behind and to one side.
Mark a wide initial support gate and an inside secondary gate.
Position a coach or passive defender who can close the first gate.
Place a receiver beyond the secondary gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves forward through the central lane.
The support player begins an outside support run.
The coach either leaves the outside gate open or closes it with a visual signal.
When the gate remains open, the support player continues through it and receives.
When the gate closes, the support player decelerates, plants and redirects underneath the ball carrier.
The ball carrier scans and handballs into the available running lane.
The support player receives at speed and disposes to the forward receiver.
Players rotate through each role.
Repeat from both sides.
coachingPoints: Begin with a genuine outside support run.
Scan the gate and the ball carrier continuously.
Recognise the closed lane early.
Decelerate before redirecting.
Do not cut directly across the ball carrier’s feet.
Communicate the new support line.
Enter the second lane with forward momentum.
The ball carrier must delay release until the new lane is clear.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the support player commits to the initial run.
Whether the gate closure is recognised early.
Whether the switchback is balanced.
Whether safe spacing is maintained around the ball carrier.
Whether the second receiving line remains forward.
progressions: Use a live defender to close either lane.
Allow the support player to select a third option.
Remove the marked gates.
Continue into an overlap after the switchback.
Add a kick to a leading forward.
regressions: Predetermine whether the first gate is open or closed.
successIndicators: Present a genuine first support option.
Recognise when that lane is unavailable.
Receive in a useful second position.
matchApplication: Support lanes frequently close as defenders shift. Effective players do not stop moving; they redirect into another space and remain connected to the ball carrier.

title: Check Lead and Turn-Out
objective: Teach players to present towards the football, recognise pressure arriving from behind and turn away into open space after receiving.
groundSize: Channels approximately 20 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position a feeder at one end of the channel.
Place a receiver approximately 12 metres away.
Position a controlled defender one metre behind the receiver.
Mark left and right turn-out gates beside the receiver.
Place a finishing target beyond each gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver leads directly towards the feeder.
The defender trails under controlled pressure.
The feeder delivers a kick or handball to the receiver.
Before receiving, the player scans over one shoulder to locate the defender.
The player takes possession and decelerates under control.
The player pivots or turns away from the defender through the open gate.
The player accelerates towards the corresponding finishing target.
The player disposes and rotates to the target position.
The defender becomes the next receiver.
coachingPoints: Lead strongly towards the football.
Scan before possession arrives.
Present the body between the defender and football.
Cushion the mark or reception.
Keep the feet active after taking possession.
Turn away from pressure rather than back into it.
Protect the football during the turn.
Accelerate after clearing the defender.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver scans before possession.
Whether the body protects the football.
Whether the player stops safely.
Whether the turn matches the defender’s position.
Whether acceleration follows the turn immediately.
progressions: Allow the defender to apply controlled body pressure.
Remove the marked turn-out gates.
Add a second defender closing one side.
Require a kick after turning.
Allow the receiver to release immediately to support instead of turning.
regressions: Allow the player to stop fully before turning.
successIndicators: Protect the football from trailing pressure.
matchApplication: A check lead is common when presenting through congestion or towards a ball carrier. The receiving player must identify pressure and turn into the safe side rather than being trapped immediately after possession.

title: Bounce-and-Accelerate Lane Change
primarySkill: Changing running lane after a bounce
objective: Develop the ability to complete a legal bounce, scan available space and accelerate into a new running lane without losing control of the football.
groundSize: Movement lanes approximately 25 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours.
setup:
Mark a straight entry lane and a central bounce zone.
Place left, centre and right exit gates beyond the bounce zone.
Position a coach with corresponding colour signals.
Place a finishing target beyond the gates.
Players begin with a football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player accelerates through the entry lane carrying the football.
Before reaching the bounce zone, the player scans the coach.
The player completes a legal bounce inside the zone.
As the football returns, the coach displays an exit colour.
The player gathers cleanly and changes running line towards the nominated gate.
The player accelerates through the gate.
The player disposes to the finishing target.
Players rotate and repeat.
Complete two or three repetitions through each gate.
coachingPoints: Scan before beginning the bounce.
Bounce the football slightly forward into the running path.
Keep the ball under control rather than forcing maximum speed.
Gather with both hands where possible.
Lower the hips before changing direction.
Use the first post-bounce step to begin the lane change.
Reaccelerate after selecting the gate.
Prepare the final disposal early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player scans before looking down.
Whether the bounce supports continued movement.
Whether the gather is clean.
Whether the lane change begins immediately.
Whether the player accelerates after the direction change.
progressions: Add a passive defender closing one gate.
Use an unpredictable football bounce.
Require the player to select the open rather than called gate.
Add a chasing defender.
Finish with a running kick.
regressions: Hand the football to a coach instead of disposing.
successIndicators: Complete a controlled bounce at speed.
matchApplication: Ball carriers often need to bounce while approaching defensive pressure. The ability to use the bounce as part of a lane change prevents the player from becoming predictable or trapped on a straight running line.

title: Traffic Weave and Clean Exit
objective: Develop the ability to move through a changing group of players, avoid collisions and identify a clean exit while maintaining possession.
groundSize: One grid approximately 15 × 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Create a rectangular grid with three exit gates at the far end.
Position four to six traffic players inside the grid.
Traffic players move continuously along assigned horizontal or diagonal lines.
One ball carrier begins at the entry gate.
Place a target beyond each exit.
howTheDrillWorks:
Traffic players begin moving through the grid at controlled speed.
The ball carrier enters with the football in two hands.
The player scans ahead and selects a path between the moving players.
The player may change pace, alter direction or pause briefly to allow a lane to open.
Traffic players do not deliberately block or tackle.
The ball carrier exits through any clear gate.
The player accelerates after clearing the traffic.
The player disposes to the corresponding target.
Rotate ball carriers and traffic players regularly.
coachingPoints: Scan several metres ahead rather than focusing on the nearest player.
Keep the football secure in two hands.
Use small adjustments instead of unnecessary large cuts.
Change pace to arrive after a traffic player has passed.
Avoid moving directly behind another player without an exit plan.
Maintain awareness of players approaching from the side.
Accelerate once a clear path is identified.
Communicate when moving through shared space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player scans beyond the nearest obstacle.
Whether movement choices avoid collisions.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether pace changes are used effectively.
Whether the player accelerates after exiting.
progressions: Allow one traffic player to provide shadow pressure.
Increase traffic speed.
Close one exit gate during the run.
Add a teammate as a release option.
Require a bounce inside the grid.
regressions: Reduce the number of traffic players.
matchApplication: Australian football players regularly move through congestion created by teammates and opponents. Efficient traffic navigation preserves possession and helps a player escape without wasting movement.

title: Moving Target Lead Adjustment
primarySkill: Adjusting a lead to a changing target
objective: Develop the ability to alter a lead when the ball carrier changes position or the original receiving lane becomes unavailable.
groundSize: Areas approximately 25 × 18 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position a ball carrier in a central starting zone.
Mark three possible ball-carrier movement points: left, centre and right.
Position a leading player approximately 18 metres away.
Mark two receiving gates.
Place a finishing target beyond the leading area.
howTheDrillWorks:
The leading player begins an initial movement towards one receiving gate.
At the same time, the ball carrier moves to one of the three nominated points.
The leading player scans and adjusts the running line to remain visible and accessible.
The player may continue the original lead, curve the run or decelerate and redirect.
The ball carrier delivers once the receiving window opens.
The player marks and immediately turns towards the finishing target.
The player disposes and rotates to the finishing position.
The ball carrier becomes the next leader.
Repeat with varied ball-carrier movements.
coachingPoints: Scan the ball carrier before and during the lead.
Avoid committing to a path that removes the passing angle.
Adjust early rather than making a late emergency turn.
Use curved movement to stay visible.
Maintain speed where possible.
Communicate the adjusted target.
Present the hands clearly.
Continue movement after receiving.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the leader scans during movement.
Whether the lead responds to the ball carrier’s location.
Whether the player maintains a useful passing angle.
Whether adjustments remain balanced.
Whether the football is delivered at the correct time.
progressions: Add a defender tracking the leader.
Allow the ball carrier to move freely.
Add a second competing lead.
Remove the receiving gates.
Require play-on after the mark.
regressions: Practise without a defender or final target.
successIndicators: Scan the ball carrier throughout the lead.
matchApplication: Leads must adjust when ball carriers are forced sideways, delayed by pressure or change their intended disposal line. Players who adapt preserve possession options and prevent attacking movement from becoming disconnected.

title: Multi-Cue Movement Chain
primarySkill: Linking movement responses to changing cues
objective: Develop the ability to complete several different movement actions in sequence while responding accurately to changing visual information.
groundSize: One 20 × 15-metre grid for every four to five players.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Divide the grid into four connected movement zones.
Zone one contains forward and backward movement markers.
Zone two contains left and right change-of-direction gates.
Zone three contains a bounce zone.
Zone four contains three finishing gates.
Position a coach where all zones are visible.
Each player begins with a football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player enters zone one and responds to a forward or backward cue.
The player transitions into zone two.
The coach displays a left or right cue and the player changes direction accordingly.
The player enters zone three and completes a legal bounce.
During the bounce, the coach identifies the finishing gate.
The player gathers, reorients and accelerates through the selected gate.
The player disposes to a target beyond the gate.
Players rotate after every repetition.
Complete four to six repetitions with varied cue combinations.
coachingPoints: Process one cue without forgetting the next movement requirement.
Maintain a balanced stance between actions.
Decelerate before major direction changes.
Keep the football secure in two hands between skills.
Scan whenever the football is under control.
Avoid rushing ahead of the cue.
Accelerate decisively once the final option is known.
Preserve disposal quality at the end of the chain.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether cues are processed accurately.
Whether movement quality declines across the sequence.
Whether players remain balanced between actions.
Whether the football stays secure.
Whether the final disposal remains accurate.
progressions: Reduce the time between cues.
Add a passive defender in the finishing zone.
Allow two players to operate simultaneously.
Replace colour cues with tactical player movements.
Add a scoring consequence for incorrect decisions.
successIndicators: Maintain movement technique across the chain.
matchApplication: Match movement rarely consists of one isolated action. Players must repeatedly accelerate, stop, redirect, bounce, scan and dispose as the situation changes around them.

title: Movement Integration Match-Flow Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated movement during continuous football flow
objective: Assess whether players can apply the chapter’s fundamental and movement-stage skills within a continuous, football-specific possession sequence.
groundSize: An area approximately 50 × 35 metres divided into five connected zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Create five connected zones:
Movement Start Zone: A player responds to a directional cue and accelerates.
Lead Zone: A second player creates separation using a curved, V-cut, double or blind-side lead.
Reorientation Zone: The receiver turns into attack after possession.
Support Zone: Teammates provide an overlap, underlap, arc or switchback run.
Exit Zone: The final ball carrier selects one of three gates and disposes to a target.
Position one controlled defender in the lead zone.
Position one controlled defender in the exit zone.
Divide players across the five zones.
Use Developing, Competent and Advanced ratings.
Assess movement quality, timing, scanning and football execution.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player responds to a visual cue and accelerates from the start zone.
The player receives and disposes to a teammate creating separation in the lead zone.
The leading player marks or receives, scans and reorients towards attack.
A support player presents through an overlap, underlap, arc or switchback movement.
The receiver selects the appropriate support option and disposes into the running path.
The support player carries towards the exit zone.
The final defender closes one gate.
The ball carrier scans and selects an available exit using acceleration, pace change or direction change.
The player disposes to the finishing target.
All players follow the football and rotate forward one position.
If a disposal misses its target, the sequence resets from the zone where possession was lost.
Each player completes at least two repetitions in different roles.
Coaches record individual strengths and priority development areas.
coachingPoints: Begin every action from a balanced movement position.
Scan before and during movement.
Create genuine separation rather than moving for appearance.
Maintain speed when receiving whenever possible.
Reorient towards attack immediately after possession.
Select support movement according to available space.
Deliver the football into the receiver’s forward path.
Protect the football when pressure approaches.
Use the simplest effective escape action.
Continue moving after every disposal.
Preserve technical quality through the entire sequence.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Athletic stance and readiness.
Quality of first-step acceleration.
Timing and effectiveness of leads.
Deceleration and change-of-direction control.
Body orientation when receiving.
Selection and timing of support runs.
Communication between players.
Football protection during movement.
Accuracy to moving targets.
Decision making in the exit zone.
Continued support after disposal.
Technical consistency across repeated efforts.
progressions: Increase the defenders’ pressure.
Remove the marked zones and gates.
Introduce a turnover transition when defenders win possession.
Add scoreboard and time consequences.
Require the final possession to become an inside-50 entry.
Assess players by position-specific movement responsibilities.
regressions: Predetermine the lead and support movements.
Allow a reset between each phase.
Reduce the number of simultaneous movement options.
successIndicators: React and accelerate from balanced positions.
Provide correctly timed and spaced support.
Select movement options based on available space.
Maintain movement quality through repeated sequences.
matchApplication: The assessment replicates continuous Australian football movement from initial possession through leading, receiving, support running and escape from pressure. It determines whether players can transfer isolated movement skills into connected team ball flow.

title: Shadow Pressure Escape Lane
objective: Develop the ability to recognise trailing pressure and use changes of pace, angle or direction to create separation while maintaining possession.
groundSize: Channels approximately 18 metres long and 6 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours.
setup:
Create several rectangular movement channels.
Mark one entry gate and two exit gates at the opposite end.
Position one attacker at the entry gate with a football.
Position one defender one metre behind the attacker.
Restrict the defender to shadow pressure without tackling.
Place a receiver five metres beyond the exit gates.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker enters the channel carrying the football in two hands.
The defender follows and attempts to remain within touching distance without making contact.
The attacker scans the defender’s position by checking over either shoulder.
The attacker uses a change of pace, running angle or controlled direction change to create separation.
The attacker exits through either gate.
The defender continues chasing but may not tackle or touch the attacker.
The attacker disposes to the receiver after clearing the gate.
Players rotate from attacker to receiver, receiver to defender and defender to the waiting line.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Check the defender’s position without losing forward vision.
Keep the football in two hands until the escape line is clear.
Use a noticeable change of speed rather than running at one pace.
Avoid drifting sideways without creating forward separation.
Transfer the football away from the defender’s side.
Make one decisive movement rather than several small evasions.
Accelerate for at least three steps after the escape.
Prepare the disposal before reaching the receiver.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker checks the defender’s position.
Whether the escape action matches the pressure line.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether the attacker creates measurable separation.
Whether acceleration continues after the escape.
Whether the final disposal remains accurate.
progressions: Allow the defender to make a two-hand touch.
Narrow the channel.
Close one exit gate during the run.
Require a legal bounce before escaping.
Add a second receiver and require a disposal decision.
regressions: Reduce the defender to jogging speed.
successIndicators: Protect the football from the pressure side.
matchApplication: Ball carriers are frequently chased from behind after a turnover, ground-ball win or handball receive. Recognising trailing pressure allows the player to avoid being run down and retain forward momentum.

title: Closing-Angle Evasion
objective: Teach ball carriers to recognise the angle of an approaching defender and attack the space outside the defender’s closing line.
groundSize: Channels approximately 16 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Mark an entry gate at one end of the channel.
Place three exit gates across the opposite end.
Position the attacker at the entry with a football.
Position the defender at either front corner of the channel.
The defender begins four metres from the attacker’s running line.
Place a target player beyond the exits.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker enters the channel at controlled running speed.
The defender begins at the same time and closes diagonally towards the attacker.
The attacker scans the defender’s hips and closing angle.
The attacker decides whether to accelerate outside the defender, cut behind the defender’s line or use a body feint before escaping.
The defender attempts to make a two-hand touch.
The attacker scores by exiting through any gate without being touched.
The attacker disposes to the target after exiting.
Players swap roles after each repetition.
Alternate the defender’s starting corner.
coachingPoints: Identify where the defender’s momentum is travelling.
Avoid running directly towards the defender’s chest.
Attack the defender’s outside shoulder when space exists.
Cut behind the defender only after the defender commits past the ball line.
Keep the football in two hands during the decision.
Transfer the football away from the pressure side.
Accelerate immediately after changing the running line.
Keep the escape movement forward whenever possible.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker recognises the defender’s closing line.
Whether the movement option suits that angle.
Whether the attacker avoids unnecessary contact.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether the attacker accelerates after the decision.
Whether the defender closes under control.
progressions: Allow controlled tackling appropriate to the group.
Reduce the channel width.
Add a recovering defender from behind.
Close one exit gate.
Require a kick to a moving target after the escape.
successIndicators: Select the space outside the closing line.
matchApplication: Defenders often approach from an angle rather than directly in front. Ball carriers who recognise the closing line can attack the defender’s weak side and avoid being forced into contact or towards the boundary.

title: Two-Hand Touch Corridor Break
objective: Develop the ability to beat controlled frontal pressure and maintain forward movement through a narrow corridor.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 18 metres long and 6 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Mark a narrow rectangular corridor.
Position the attacker at one end with a football.
Position one defender six metres inside the corridor.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Place a receiver five metres beyond the gate.
The defender uses two-hand touch only.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker enters the corridor with the football in two hands.
The defender advances to close the attacker’s forward line.
The attacker may use acceleration, a pace change, sidestep or body feint.
The attacker attempts to pass the defender without being touched with two hands.
The defender may move freely but must remain controlled.
The attacker scores one point for crossing the gate and another for completing the disposal.
The defender scores one point for a legal two-hand touch before the gate.
Players rotate after each repetition.
Complete several attacks from each side of the defender.
coachingPoints: Approach with enough speed to threaten both sides.
Maintain control so the defender’s movement can be read.
Attack one shoulder rather than the centre of the defender.
Use one decisive evasion action.
Keep the football secure until clear.
Accelerate through the defender’s shoulder line.
Avoid drifting towards the boundary of the corridor.
Regain disposal posture before releasing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker carries with control.
Whether the attacker makes the defender commit.
Whether the chosen evasion is decisive.
Whether the defender applies safe pressure.
Whether the attacker retains forward momentum.
Whether the final disposal remains composed.
progressions: Narrow the corridor.
Allow controlled tackling.
Add a second defender beyond the first.
Require a bounce before the scoring gate.
Add a support player as an alternative to evasion.
successIndicators: Create a reaction from the defender.
matchApplication: The drill replicates a ball carrier attempting to break through a narrow corridor, exit a stoppage or maintain forward momentum when a defender is positioned directly ahead.

title: Contact Balance and Continue
objective: Teach players to absorb controlled body pressure, remain on their feet and continue moving into space with possession.
groundSize: Contact lanes approximately 15 metres long and 5 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Create several straight contact lanes.
Position an attacker at the start with a football.
Position a defender or coach holding a bump pad midway through the lane.
Mark a contact zone approximately three metres long.
Place a receiver beyond the finishing gate.
Establish strict contact intensity before beginning.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker enters the lane carrying the football securely.
The defender or pad holder approaches from one side inside the contact zone.
The attacker lowers the body position and prepares for controlled shoulder-to-shoulder pressure.
The attacker keeps the feet moving through contact.
The attacker protects the football on the side away from pressure.
After contact, the attacker regains full running posture and accelerates through the finishing gate.
The attacker disposes to the receiver.
Players rotate roles after each repetition.
Repeat with pressure arriving from both sides.
coachingPoints: Establish a stable body position before contact.
Keep the knees flexed and the feet active.
Present the shoulder and side of the body rather than the chest.
Keep the head away from the contact line.
Secure the football close to the protected side.
Avoid extending the arm into the defender.
Continue stepping through the pressure.
Accelerate once balance is regained.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether contact remains controlled and legal.
Whether the attacker prepares before contact.
Whether the feet continue moving.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether the player regains balance quickly.
Whether disposal quality is maintained.
progressions: Replace the pad with controlled player contact.
Increase the approach angle.
Add a second pressure contact.
Require a bounce after contact.
Add a live support option after the pressure.
regressions: Allow a full reset before the final disposal.
matchApplication: Players often receive body pressure while collecting a football, breaking from congestion or running beside an opponent. Maintaining balance allows possession to continue rather than ending with a fall or rushed disposal.

title: Boundary Pressure Turn-In or Turn-Out
objective: Develop the ability to assess pressure near the boundary and choose whether to turn inside, continue outside or release the football.
groundSize: Boundary channels approximately 20 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Mark one sideline to represent the boundary.
Position an attacker five metres inside the boundary with a football.
Position a defender one metre behind and inside the attacker.
Place one target further down the boundary and another target inside the ground.
Mark an inside turn gate and an outside continuation gate.
Use two-hand touch pressure only.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker begins moving along the boundary.
The defender applies trailing and inside pressure.
The attacker scans the defender and both targets.
If the defender protects the inside, the attacker may continue outside and dispose down the line.
If the defender overcommits towards the boundary, the attacker may decelerate and turn inside.
The attacker may also release immediately if a target becomes available before pressure arrives.
The defender attempts a controlled two-hand touch.
The attacker scores for choosing an available option and completing the disposal.
Rotate attackers, defenders and targets.
coachingPoints: Use the boundary as information rather than becoming trapped by it.
Scan inside before receiving or carrying.
Keep the football on the side away from the defender.
Do not turn inside blindly.
Decelerate before attempting a sharp inside turn.
Continue outside when the defender has protected the corridor.
Release early when the disposal is safer than evasion.
Accelerate after turning into the ground.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker scans the inside target.
Whether the decision matches the defender’s position.
Whether the boundary is used intelligently.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether the attacker avoids turning into pressure.
Whether the selected disposal is accurate.
progressions: Allow controlled tackling.
Add a second inside defender.
Remove the marked gates.
Allow the boundary target to lead.
Continue into a second possession phase.
regressions: Increase the space from the boundary.
successIndicators: Recognise the boundary and pressure relationship.
Scan inside and down the line.
Select an available escape or disposal.
matchApplication: Players receiving near the boundary must quickly decide whether to use the line, turn back into the ground or release possession. Poor decisions can result in tackles, boundary stoppages or turnovers in dangerous positions.

title: Stoppage Exit Under Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to win possession in a confined area, identify an exit lane and accelerate away from controlled stoppage pressure.
groundSize: One central contest circle eight metres in diameter with four exit gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Mark a central circular congestion area.
Place four exit gates around the outside.
Position one attacking player in the centre.
Position two controlled pressure players nearby.
Place one feeder outside the circle.
Position one receiver beyond each gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder delivers a bouncing or rolling football into the centre.
The attacker moves to collect while the two pressure players close space.
Pressure players may use controlled body positioning and two-hand touch but may not tackle initially.
The attacker secures the football and scans the exit gates.
One gate is closed by a coach’s colour signal.
The attacker uses acceleration, a pivot, sidestep or body protection to exit through an open gate.
The attacker disposes to the receiver outside the gate.
Pressure players score by making a two-hand touch before the attacker exits.
Rotate roles after two repetitions.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with a low, balanced body position.
Secure possession before attempting to escape.
Keep the head and eyes active around the contest.
Use the first step to move away from pressure.
Avoid running towards both pressure players.
Protect the football on the far side.
Take the shortest available exit.
Dispose immediately once clear if the receiver is available.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker secures possession cleanly.
Whether the player scans before selecting an exit.
Whether the first step moves away from pressure.
Whether balance is maintained through contact.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether the disposal occurs after sufficient separation.

Add a second attacking support player.
Close two exit gates.
Require a handball release rather than carrying through the gate.
Add an immediate turnover transition.
successIndicators: Move away from pressure with the first step.
matchApplication: The drill replicates a player winning possession at a stoppage and attempting to exit congestion before being tackled. Efficient movement helps convert contested possession into effective team possession.

title: Two-versus-One Evasion and Release
objective: Develop the ability to engage a defender and decide whether to evade directly or release the football to a supporting teammate.
groundSize: Channels approximately 18 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Mark one starting gate and two scoring gates.
Position one ball carrier at the start with a football.
Position one support player behind and to either side.
Place one defender six metres ahead.
The defender uses two-hand touch pressure.
Mark a support lane on each side.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier and support player enter together.
The defender advances and decides whether to pressure the ball carrier or protect the support option.
The ball carrier scans the defender’s position.
If the defender commits to the ball carrier, the football is released to the support runner.
If the defender protects the support player or remains passive, the ball carrier may evade and attack an exit.
The support player adjusts the running line to remain available.
The attacking pair scores by crossing either gate in possession.
The defender scores with a legal two-hand touch.
Rotate all three roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Carry forward strongly enough to engage the defender.
Keep the support player behind and outside the football.
Avoid releasing before the defender commits.
Use evasion when the defender gives the ball carrier clear space.
Handball into the support player’s forward path.
Communicate the support side.
Continue moving after releasing.
Do not force an evasion when the support option is clearly safer.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier draws the defender.
Whether the support player maintains useful spacing.
Whether the decision matches the defender’s action.
Whether the handball leads the support player.
Whether both attackers continue moving after the decision.
progressions: Allow controlled tackling.
Add a recovering defender.
Remove marked support lanes.
Add a second support player.
Continue into a three-versus-two phase.
regressions: Predetermine whether the defender commits or holds.
Allow the support player to begin closer.
successIndicators: Deliver into the support runner’s path.
Cross an exit gate in possession.
matchApplication: Ball carriers must constantly choose between taking on an opponent and using a teammate. Effective decisions create numerical advantage and reduce unnecessary tackles or turnovers.

title: Recovering Defender Chase Escape
objective: Develop the ability to recognise a recovering defender approaching from behind or the side and escape before the defender can apply effective pressure.
groundSize: Channels approximately 25 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position the attacker at the start with a football.
Position the defender three metres behind and slightly to one side.
Mark three exit gates 15 metres ahead.
Position a receiver beyond the gates.
The defender uses two-hand touch only.
Ensure adequate run-off space beyond the channel.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker begins accelerating with the football.
The defender starts one second later and chases.
The attacker performs one or two shoulder checks to locate the defender.
The attacker selects a gate based on the defender’s recovery line.
The attacker may accelerate, change pace or redirect once.
The defender attempts a two-hand touch before the exit.
The attacker disposes to the receiver after crossing the gate.
Players rotate roles after every repetition.
Repeat with the defender starting from both sides.
coachingPoints: Accelerate early to use the starting advantage.
Check the defender without repeatedly looking backwards.
Move away from the defender’s recovery line.
Keep the football on the far side.
Avoid a large direction change that sacrifices too much speed.
Use one controlled movement if the defender closes.
Dispose before being caught when the receiver is clearly available.
Maintain running technique under pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker uses the initial space.
Whether the shoulder check is brief and informative.
Whether the exit choice moves away from the defender.
Whether speed is maintained.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether disposal timing is appropriate.
progressions: Reduce the attacker’s starting advantage.
Allow controlled tackling.
Add a second defender ahead.
Require a bounce during the chase.
Add a return handball after the first disposal.
successIndicators: Move away from the chase line.
Escape or release before being caught.
matchApplication: Recovering defenders often chase after turnovers or broken defensive structures. Ball carriers must recognise where that pressure is coming from and act before their space disappears.

title: Congestion Exit with Live Gates
primarySkill: Selecting an escape route from live congestion
objective: Develop the ability to maintain possession inside changing congestion and identify the safest available exit under live defensive pressure.
groundSize: One grid approximately 14 × 14 metres with four exit gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Create a square grid with one gate on each side.
Position two attackers and two defenders inside.
One attacker begins with the football.
Position one receiver outside each gate.
Defenders may use controlled body positioning and two-hand touch.
The coach can close one gate with a colour signal.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with the ball carrier inside the congestion grid.
The second attacker moves to provide a support or decoy option.
Defenders pressure the ball carrier and protect likely exits.
The coach closes one gate after play begins.
The ball carrier scans and may evade, pivot, use the support player or change pace.
The attacking pair scores by carrying or handballing through an open gate to an outside receiver.
Defenders score by completing a two-hand touch, forcing an error or intercepting.
If the football changes possession, defenders immediately become attackers.
Play continues for 15–20 seconds or until the football exits.
Rotate outside receivers into the grid after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Scan before possession arrives and continue scanning after receiving.
Keep the football in two hands while options remain uncertain.
Avoid turning repeatedly without gaining space.
Use the supporting attacker to move defenders.
Attack the largest available exit rather than the nearest cone.
Protect the football through body contact.
Release when support has a cleaner path.
Accelerate decisively once an exit opens.
React immediately if possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers scan multiple gates.
Whether the supporting player creates useful movement.
Whether defenders communicate and protect space.
Whether the ball carrier avoids unnecessary turning.
Whether the exit decision is appropriate.
Whether transition occurs immediately after a turnover.
progressions: Allow legal tackling appropriate to the group.
Add another defender and attacker.
Close two gates.
Require a kick after exiting.
Introduce a scoreboard and short possession limit.
Expand into a second transition grid.
successIndicators: React quickly to changes of possession.
matchApplication: The drill replicates live congestion around stoppages, boundary contests and pressured ground balls. Players must solve a changing movement problem rather than follow a predetermined exit.

title: Pressure and Contest Movement Assessment
objective: Assess each player’s ability to apply evasion, balance, football protection and decision making against controlled match-like pressure.
groundSize: An area approximately 40 × 30 metres divided into five pressure-assessment stations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Create five assessment stations:
Trailing Pressure Escape: The player must escape a shadowing defender.
Closing-Angle Decision: The player reacts to an angled defender.
Contact Balance: The player carries through controlled body or pad pressure.
Evasion or Release: The player works with one support teammate against one defender.
Congestion Exit: The player escapes through one of several live gates.
Assign one coach or observer to each station where possible.
Use ratings of Developing, Competent or Advanced.
Assess both decision quality and movement execution.
Complete one familiarisation repetition before recording scores.
Set contact intensity appropriate to the age and experience of the group.
howTheDrillWorks:
Divide players evenly between the five stations.
Each player completes two scored repetitions at every station.
At Station 1, the attacker uses a pace or direction change to escape trailing pressure.
At Station 2, the attacker reads the defender’s approach and selects an outside or cutback exit.
At Station 3, the attacker absorbs controlled contact, remains balanced and disposes.
At Station 4, the ball carrier chooses between evasion and releasing to support.
At Station 5, the attacker scans multiple gates and escapes congestion.
Coaches score balance, scanning, decision quality, football protection, acceleration and disposal execution.
Players rotate after all group members complete the station.
Coaches provide one priority correction after the second repetition.
Complete all five stations before conducting a brief group review.
coachingPoints: Assess the decision as well as the physical movement.
Require players to scan before committing.
Check whether the selected action matches the defender’s position.
Monitor football security throughout pressure.
Observe body alignment during stopping, planting and contact.
Reward one decisive movement rather than repeated evasions.
Look for acceleration after separation is created.
Assess the player’s willingness to release when support is the safer option.
Preserve safe contact standards at every station.
Record clear individual development priorities.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Starting balance and readiness.
Awareness of defender position.
Selection of appropriate movement.
Ability to change pace or direction.
Leg and trunk control through contact.
Football protection.
Use of available support.
Acceleration after evasion.
Disposal accuracy under pressure.
Behaviour immediately after losing or releasing possession.
progressions: Repeat the assessment with match-like legal tackling.
Compare results across multiple testing dates.
Add positional versions for inside midfielders, wings, forwards and defenders.
Introduce fatigue before the second assessed repetition.
Add scoreboard and time consequences.
Continue each station into a transition phase after the initial escape.
regressions: Complete stations separately across several sessions.
Remove contact from the balance station.
Allow a reset before the final disposal.
successIndicators: Choose an effective escape or release option.
Create separation with one decisive movement.
Demonstrate safe and repeatable movement technique.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can transfer evasion and movement technique into pressured Australian football situations. It identifies whether a player can retain possession, escape contact, use support and continue ball movement when time and space are restricted.

title: Dual-Side Pressure Ball Carry
primarySkill: Protecting possession against pressure from either side
objective: Develop the ability to recognise which side pressure is arriving from, transfer the football to safety and continue moving into available space.
groundSize: Movement channels approximately 18 metres long and 8 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Create a rectangular movement channel with one entry gate and two exit gates.
Position one attacker at the entry with a football.
Place one pressure player on each side of the channel.
Pressure players begin approximately three metres ahead and two metres outside the attacker’s running line.
Position a receiver beyond the exit gates.
Pressure players initially use controlled shoulder contact or bump pads only.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker enters the channel carrying the football in two hands.
One pressure player advances towards the attacker while the other holds position.
The attacker scans and identifies the active pressure side.
The attacker transfers the football to the side furthest from pressure.
The attacker positions the body between the defender and football.
The attacker changes running line towards the open exit gate.
The pressure player applies controlled shoulder-to-shoulder pressure.
The attacker keeps the feet moving, exits the channel and disposes to the receiver.
Players rotate through attacker, pressure and receiver roles.
Repeat with pressure arriving unpredictably from both sides.
coachingPoints: Carry in two hands until the pressure side is recognised.
Transfer the football early rather than during contact.
Turn the torso slightly to protect possession.
Keep the head and eyes forward after identifying pressure.
Maintain a low, balanced running position.
Avoid extending the arm into the defender.
Change running lane away from the contact line.
Accelerate after clearing pressure.
Reorganise the football before disposing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker identifies the correct pressure side.
Whether the hand transfer occurs early enough.
Whether body position legally protects the football.
Whether balance is maintained through contact.
Whether the attacker moves towards the open gate.
Whether disposal quality is retained.
progressions: Allow either pressure player to engage.
Permit both defenders to close at controlled intensity.
Replace bump pads with legal player body contact.
Add a recovering defender beyond the exit.
Require a kick after escaping.
regressions: Allow a full reset before disposal.
matchApplication: Ball carriers often receive pressure from changing sides when exiting stoppages, collecting loose footballs or running through traffic. Early recognition and safe football transfer help preserve possession through contact.

title: Three-Sixty Pressure Escape
primarySkill: Escaping pressure from an unknown direction
objective: Develop the ability to scan around possession, recognise pressure from any direction and escape through the safest available space.
groundSize: One circular grid approximately 10 metres in diameter for every six players.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Mark a circular grid with one coloured gate at each compass point.
Position one attacker in the centre with a football.
Place two defenders on opposite sides of the circle.
Position one receiver outside each gate.
Defenders begin three metres from the attacker.
Use two-hand touch pressure only.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker begins in the centre holding the football in two hands.
On the coach’s signal, one or both defenders begin closing from their starting positions.
The attacker scans around the full circle.
The coach closes one gate with a colour signal after pressure begins.
The attacker selects an open gate away from the strongest pressure.
The attacker may pivot, change pace, sidestep or accelerate directly.
Defenders attempt a controlled two-hand touch.
The attacker scores by exiting an open gate and disposing to the receiver.
Defenders score by touching the attacker or forcing an error.
Rotate roles after every two repetitions.
coachingPoints: Scan before the defenders arrive.
Keep the football secure in two hands.
Identify pressure direction and available space together.
Avoid turning blindly into a second defender.
Use the shortest safe movement to reach an exit.
Pivot compactly rather than spinning repeatedly.
Accelerate once the exit is selected.
Use a receiver when disposal is safer than carrying.
Maintain awareness after the first defender is beaten.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacker scans before committing.
Whether the selected exit moves away from pressure.
Whether the player recognises the second defender.
Whether the pivot or direction change remains balanced.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether the outside receiver is used effectively.
progressions: Allow controlled tackling.
Add a third defender.
Close two gates.
Place one supporting attacker inside the circle.
Introduce immediate turnover transition.
successIndicators: Complete the disposal outside the grid.
matchApplication: Players winning possession in congestion may have pressure arriving from behind, beside and in front. Effective scanning and compact movement allow them to avoid blind turns and escape through the safest available space.

title: Ground-Ball Gather and Immediate Evasion
primarySkill: Moving from ground-ball collection into evasion
objective: Teach players to collect a ground football cleanly, identify immediate pressure and use their first movement to escape rather than becoming stationary.
groundSize: Channels approximately 16 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Mark a central collection zone with an exit gate on each side.
Position one attacker five metres from the collection zone.
Position one defender at either side of the zone.
Place a feeder opposite the attacker with several footballs.
Position a receiver beyond each exit.
Defenders initially apply two-hand touch and controlled body pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls or bounces the football into the collection zone.
The attacker approaches with a low, balanced body position.
As the attacker reaches the football, one defender begins closing.
The attacker gathers the football cleanly in two hands.
The attacker identifies the defender’s position during the approach.
The first step after collection moves away from pressure.
The attacker protects the football and accelerates through an exit gate.
The attacker disposes to the receiver.
Rotate attacker, defender, receiver and feeder roles.
Repeat with pressure arriving from both sides and varied football movement.
coachingPoints: Scan before lowering the head towards the football.
Approach at a speed that permits clean collection.
Place the body behind the football.
Gather in two hands.
Stay low for the first two steps after collection.
Move away from pressure immediately.
Keep the football on the protected side.
Avoid standing upright before accelerating.
Dispose once balance and separation have been established.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player scans before collecting.
Whether the football is gathered cleanly.
Whether the first movement avoids the defender.
Whether the player remains balanced and low.
Whether possession is protected.
Whether acceleration follows the collection.

Add a second defender.
Deliver an unpredictable bouncing football.

title: Mark, Play On and Escape Pressure
primarySkill: Playing on from a mark into available space

groundSize: Areas approximately 22 × 15 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position one kicker at the start of the area.

Place a finishing target beyond each gate.
The defender applies controlled closing pressure after the mark.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker delivers the football to the receiver.
While the football is in flight, the receiver scans the defender and both play-on gates.
The receiver completes the mark.
The defender closes one side after the mark is taken.
The receiver identifies the open gate.
The receiver pivots, steps off the mark and accelerates through the gate.
The receiver disposes to the corresponding finishing target.
The defender attempts a two-hand touch after the player leaves the mark.
Players rotate through kicker, receiver, defender and target roles.
Repeat from both sides.
coachingPoints: Scan while the football is travelling.
Mark with the hands and maintain a balanced landing.
Keep the feet active after the mark.
Identify which side the defender is closing.
Use a compact pivot or first step.
Protect the football while leaving the mark.

Use the stationary disposal when it is the safer option.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player scans before marking.
Whether the landing position permits movement.
Whether the correct side is selected.
Whether the player leaves the mark decisively.
Whether possession remains protected.
Whether the player recognises when not to play on.

Remove the marked gates.
Require a running kick.
Add a support handball option.

title: Pressure Receive and One-Step Release
primarySkill: Rapid disposal after receiving under pressure

setup:

The defender uses two-hand touch pressure.

The feeder handballs to the receiver.
As the football travels, the coach or feeder calls a target colour.
The defender begins closing from behind.
The receiver catches, takes no more than one organising step and disposes to the nominated target.
The receiver may pivot or release from the receiving side depending on the target.
The defender attempts a two-hand touch after the catch.
Players rotate clockwise after each repetition.
Repeat with the defender starting from different angles.
coachingPoints: Scan both targets before the football arrives.
Present the hands early.
Receive in front of the body.
Keep the feet active.
Use one efficient organising step.
Turn the hips towards the target.
Protect the football during the transfer.
Release before pressure reaches the body.
Maintain disposal accuracy rather than rushing blindly.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver scans before possession.
Whether the football is caught cleanly.
Whether footwork efficiently aligns the body.
Whether the correct target is selected.
Whether release occurs before contact.
Whether handball accuracy remains high.

title: Split-Two Defender Escape
primarySkill: Escaping between or around two defenders
objective: Teach players to assess the spacing and movement of two defenders and determine whether to attack the split or escape around the outside.
groundSize: Channels approximately 20 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Mark one entry gate and three exit gates.
Position the attacker at the entry with a football.
Place two defenders six metres ahead and approximately four metres apart.
Position one receiver beyond the exits.
Defenders apply two-hand touch pressure.
Vary the defenders’ starting width across repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker enters at controlled speed.
Both defenders advance while maintaining or changing their spacing.
The attacker scans the gap between them and the outside space.
If the defenders separate too far, the attacker accelerates through the split.
If the defenders close the split, the attacker uses a pace or direction change to escape outside.
The attacker may use a body feint to move one defender.
Defenders attempt a controlled two-hand touch.
The attacker exits through a gate and disposes to the receiver.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
Repeat with varied defender spacing and movement.
coachingPoints: See both defenders rather than locking onto one.
Assess whether the central gap is widening or closing.
Attack the split only when it can be reached before the defenders connect.
Use one defender to obstruct the other where possible.

setup:

Evasion and Pressure Phase

Match Application Phase
